newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines' Ramos out of hospital, looks fit.
newsitem.headline: Philippines' Ramos out of hospital, looks fit.

text.p: Philippine President Fidel Ramos checked out of hospital on Thursday, three days after critical surgery, and said he was ready to work and play golf again.

A crowd of hospital staff and visitors cheered when the 68-year-old Ramos, smiling and dressed in a dark jacket, came down to the lobby of the Makati Medical Centre along with his wife Amelita and walked unaided to a black limousine escorted by his doctors.
"I am feeling very, very well," he told reporters before being driven to his residence for a brief rest before proceeding to the Malacanang presidential palace to start working on state papers.
"What's that?" he said, grinning, when asked if he would slow down.
"Very soon," Ramos, an avid golfer, shouted back when a reporter asked when he would play golf again.
"He'll play golf in about 10 days' time," his chief doctor and hospital director Raul Fores told Reuters.
But Fores said he had advised Ramos, who follows a rigorous 18-hour daily work schedule, to cut down his pace and sleep longer.
"He is 68 years old. He cannot follow the schedule of a 20-year-old which was what he was doing. He wan't sleeping enough," Fores said.
Fores blamed the high cholesterol level in the president's blood system, which prompted the emergency operation, on a diet of too much rich food.

Ramos underwent surgery on Monday to remove a cholesterol blockage in his right carotid artery, one of the major passages for blood flowing to the brain. Officials had said the affliction could have been life-threatening.
But doctors have said the operation was successfully performed and there should be no recurrence of the illness. They said blood checks on Thursday morning had shown lower cholesterol levels.
